axes.label: Weight
axes.desc: Where the body's weight lives: pulled up and away from the floor, or yielded into it.

axes.label: Torso
axes.desc: How much the spine bends, contracts and twists instead of staying a vertical column.

axes.label: Dynamics
axes.desc: The energy shape of a phrase: smooth and continuous, or sharp attacks and stops.

axes.label: Floor
axes.desc: How much of the technique happens on, into and through the floor.

axes.label: Initiation
axes.desc: Where movement starts: hands, feet and points in space, or the pelvis, breath and centre.

axes.label: Structure
axes.desc: A fixed vocabulary taught as set exercises, or tasks and principles you improvise from.

axes.label: Balance
axes.desc: Whether balance is something to keep, or something to give up and catch again.

axes.label: Contact
axes.desc: How much the practice depends on touching, leaning on and carrying another body.

techniques.name: Graham
principles: Floor work as a warm-up sequence
techniques.why: The contraction is a sharp, pelvis-driven curve of the spine, practised as a fixed class order that starts seated on the floor.

techniques.name: Horton
principles: Long lines through the whole body
Studies built for strength and flexibility
techniques.why: A strongly codified anatomical system; the torso works in straight planes (flat back, lateral T) more than curves.

techniques.name: Limón
techniques.why: Built on Humphrey's 'arc between two deaths': giving in to gravity and suspending out of it, on the breath.

techniques.name: Dunham
principles: Isolations of hips, ribs and shoulders
Afro-Caribbean roots with ballet and modern training
techniques.why: Grounded, pelvis-centred and rhythmic, with an articulate, isolating torso taught through set progressions.

techniques.name: Cunningham
principles: Curve, arch, tilt and twist of the upper back
techniques.why: Upright and quick on ballet legs; the back bends in five set directions while balance stays sharply controlled.

techniques.name: Butoh
principles: The body being moved rather than moving
techniques.why: Deeply grounded and almost continuously slow; worked through images rather than a fixed step vocabulary.

techniques.name: Release Technique
techniques.founder: Joan Skinner, Mary Fulkerson and others
techniques.why: Lets go of held tension and trusts weight and momentum; taught through images and principles more than set steps.

techniques.name: Contact Improvisation
techniques.why: An improvised duet form whose whole subject is the moving point of contact and shared weight.

techniques.name: Improvisation Technologies
principles: Points, lines and planes in space
techniques.why: Movement starts from imagined points and lines around the body, then is improvised with clear operations.

techniques.name: Flying Low
principles: Spiralling in and out of the floor
Moving fast close to the ground
techniques.why: Very low, very fast travel in and out of the floor, organised from the centre in spirals.

techniques.name: Gaga
techniques.why: Improvised from spoken images, with a very fluid, articulate spine and a wide dynamic range.

techniques.name: Countertechnique
principles: Sending body parts in opposite directions
techniques.why: A set class with clear tools that uses counter-directions to go off balance safely.
